name: Controlled stand — resume the from-scratch checkpoint (watch)
hint: R12c on duck_pipeline_s2: tall, still (~0.1 mrad/tick), zero falls. What the brain does when nothing happens to it.

name: Push test — 2 N shoves on the controlled stand every 60 s (watch)
hint: The (d) test, design doc §11. 0.1 s shoves on a rotating heading; ≥ 2 N knocks it over, the scaffold rescues, c collapses and is re-earned in ~38 s. Report gives the per-shove table.

name: Envelope — 1 N shoves on the controlled stand (the catch limit)
hint: 1 N × 0.1 s is caught at 1–4° of tilt; 1.5 N is 50/50; 2 N topples. Change the force to bracket a brain's envelope; Report reads it.

name: Pipeline 1/3 — find from scratch (R13, 2 h, headless, saves the brain)
hint: Design doc §12.3/§12.6. Seed 2 stands by ~30 min (falls 8 → 3 → 1 → 0/min); other seeds fall-cycle. Tick 'battery' with seeds 1-6 for the race. ≈ 380 MB of JSONL.

name: Pipeline 2/3 — gain hunt (R11, 30 min, from the latest saved brain)
hint: Resume the find brain under R11: C norms shed, no falls, oscillation 12 → 11 mrad. Load-bearing — handing the find brain straight to R12c fails (§12.6).

name: Pipeline 3/3 — rest (R12c, 30 min, from the latest saved brain)
hint: Resume the hunted brain under R12c: the efference rests at earned stillness, |dq| 11 → 0.1 mrad/tick, c 1.00. Watch it to see the oscillation stop.

name: Wind arm — find from scratch with 0.5 N shoves every 8 s (§12.4, null)
hint: The world-with-wind lever: sub-topple shoves throughout learning. Measured null — it stands, never rests, envelope unchanged. Here to be re-run against a new idea.

name: Byte-identity reference — r3, seed 6, 300 s (headless)
hint: The guard: run it before touching code, keep the JSONL, run it again after, cmp (strip the 'cons' field if the reference predates it).

name: Scaffold — shove Pollen's standing policy (5 N every 4 s, watch)
hint: The RL reference: staggers and catches 5 N, knocked over at 10 N and stands back up. The envelope the brain is measured against.

name: Recovery harness — the stub brain that falls over (watch)
hint: A brain that fails, the scaffold that picks it up, and the hand-off between them. Tests the harness, not the substrate.
